text:
By Reesha ,
12 hours ago Photo Credit Yakima Police Department via Facebook, Du≈°an veverkolog on Unsplash and Canva ‚Äì No Roosters in Yakima Du≈°an veverkolog on Unsplash and Canva Locals react to a Facebook post reminder from the Yakima Police Department that you can‚Äôt own roosters in Yakima . The comments didn‚Äôt seem to go as expected.
Who knew that a reminder to residents that we can‚Äôt have any roosters in city limits would get such a spirited response? Certainly not me.
‚ÄúReally?! THIS is what you‚Äôre worried about?!‚Äù, replied one resident after the Yakima Police Department posted this message to their Facebook page on January 26th at 8:16 in the morning.
Another ticked off person wanted to know since the police were so concerned if they would be running around counting how many hens they had. (The post was about roosters, not hens!)
Several others piped up that their roosters identified as chickens, dogs, and ducks. Silly replies for silly times, I guess.

Photo Credit Yakima Police Department via Facebook, DusÃåan veverkolog on Unsplash and Canva Why Can‚Äôt People Have Roosters in Yakima? This ain‚Äôt Green Acres, y‚Äôall. There are city limits with city ordinances, including the one that says no roosters in town. A rooster is considered a domesticated animal that falls outside the allowed list.
"‚Äú‚ÄúPet‚Äù means a domesticated animal kept for pleasure or as a hobby rather than utility including but not limited to: fish, dogs fewer than four, cats fewer than six, hen chickens (no roosters) fewer than five, and rabbits fewer than five.‚Äù ‚Äì¬†Yakima Municipal Code 15.04.060 (D)"

Gallery Credit: Reesha Cosby Google Street View Gasperetti's and G Spot Bar Google Street View Have you been to the new Agua Tequila's Restaurant yet? The place that once was Gasperetti's Restaurant for decades is now a Mexican restaurant and bar. Google Street View The old Shopko building Google Street View The old Shopko building and parking lot became At Home and Burlington Coat Factory At Home just announced they are closing this Union Gap location. That's a bummer! Google Street View Raise your hand if you ever played bingo here! RIP Superbingo! Google Street View B-I-N-G-GONE! Now there is a furniture store and a couple of restarants. Google Street View The Westfair Shopping Center sign had a very 1970s feel to it back in the day. Google Street View What happened to all the other letters? Google Street View This is a picturesque view from the Nob Hill Bridge back in the day. Google Street View The view is still lovely but has a few modern buildings in the background. Google Street View Riase your hand if you used to get AMF's at the Old Pete's Nightclub! Pete's Nightclub Google Street View Pete's Nightclub became a fancy brunch and dinner joint. Second Street Grill. Google Street View This is what the (allegedly haunted) Sports Center used to look like back in the day. There is a neon sign of a sniper with a gun. It used to rotate! Google Street View The sniper sign guy is still there as well as a new pizza joint. Google Street View Back in the day, this used to be the downtown movie theater. Google Street View Va va voom! Now it's Orion Cinema's & Mickey's Pub. This is a 21+ establishment only. No kids allowed! Google Street View Remember when this space used to be the home of the Ihop? Google Street View Now there are some fancy new parking lots and businesses there. Google Street View Back in the day at the Old Eisenhower High School Google Street View Ike High got a million-dollar glow up! Google Street View The old Davis High School Let's go Pirates! Google Street View Davis High got a glow up! Google Street View Do you remember when there used to be a green space next to the corner of North 2nd Street and Yakima Ave? Google Street View There is a fancy restaurant in this space now. Cowiche Canyon Kitchen & Ice House Bar. Google Street View A few years back, this space on N 64th Ave looked like the edge of Farm Town, USA. Google Street View Voila! There's apartments, medical offices, and more! Google Street View This is what the Fiesta Foods lot looked like back in the day. Google Street View Now there's a Little Caesar's pizza shop and more. Google Street View This is what the new vision of the Larson Building space looked like before the public art was installed. Google Street View This is some pretty impressive public art! Google Street View Greystone This restaurant had a classic English pub feel. I miss it! Google Street View 5 North After the Greystone closed down, a new glam restaurant opened up in its place, 5 North. Google Street View Track 29 was a fun place to go, especially on Cinco de Mayo! Do you remember Tequila's? It was such a fun place to go for happy hour and great Mexican food! Shout out to Javi! Google Street View I used to love window shopping at Garden Dance! Google Street View Yakima Rotary Marketplace Track 29 was demolished and rebranded as a new place for the Downtown Farmers Market and other community events. Google Street View The Speakeasy Dive Bar Lots of pool table cues and well drinks were consumed at this iconic dive bar. Do you know what stands in this location now? (See the next pic.) Google Street View The Speakeasy was demolished and up sprang a new fancy restaurant. EZ Tiger is one of the swankiest restaurants in downtown Yakima. Google Street View Many fun and crazy memories were made by thousands of people at the old Jackson's Sportsbar & Clubhouse Lounge Google Street View The old Jackson's location is now a smaller club and a cigar bar. Google Street View This plot of land in Chesterley Park, we hardly knew ye! Google Street View Behold! The new YMCA Rotary Aquatic Center It has 2 fun slides that swing you outside of the building! Google Street View Remember Casa Mia? Me, too! Google Street View The Kabob House took over the old Casa Mia Italian Restaurant location. Google Street View Tasty Wok has taken over the old Greek restaurant location. Google Street View Remember going to Borders Books in Union Gap by the mall? RIP! I miss going here so much! It was like a best friend to me. LOL. Google Street View The old Borders Books building became a hobby hotspot named Michaels. Located right near the Valley Mall in Union Gap. Google Street View The old Comfort World building on Yakima Ave It reminds me of that appliance store in That Thing You Do movie with Tom Hanks. Google Street View The old Comfort World/Pita Pit building is now Avenida Cantina and &Tea Located on Yakima Avenue in the heart of downtown Yakima. Photo Credit Google Street View The "Palm Springs of Washington" Sign on East R Street Hate it or love it, this iconic sign visible from I-82 still remains the same after all these years.
